cards.title: Build a command without surprises
synonyms: what does the vertical bar do
cards.effect: Understand what the shell passes to each program; examples only print synthetic text.
cards.recovery: Ctrl-C cancels the current input or interrupts a foreground command. It cannot undo an overwrite or a remote action.

source.label: zsh manual
source.revision: zsh 5.9 concepts; generic, not local bindings

cards.title: Find a file without typing its path
cards.layer: Interactive shell prompt — not inside Neovim
cards.effect: A configured file picker inserts a path into the command line; it does not run that command.
cards.recovery: Esc cancels the picker. Inspect the resulting shell line; Ctrl-C clears it before execution.

source.label: fzf shell integration
source.revision: fzf 0.74.3 reference; shell hooks must be checked separately

exercise.goal: Insert a disposable file's path without typing the full path. Do not execute the completed command.
hints: Start at your shell prompt, in a small directory you know.
Type nvim followed by a space. Check the file-picker binding in this card.
Select a filename, inspect the inserted path, then Ctrl-C to discard the line.
exercise.success: You can explain why choosing a file and running the completed command are two separate actions.

cards.title: Recall a command without running it blindly
cards.effect: Recall text for inspection before execution; this guide never reads your shell history.
cards.recovery: Esc cancels a configured fzf picker; Ctrl-C discards a recalled line. Previous commands may have effects that cannot be undone.

source.label: fzf shell integration
source.revision: fzf 0.74.3 reference; recorded shell hooks are not runtime verification

cards.title: Return to a workspace without closing your work
cards.effect: Detaching leaves the session running on its host. Reattaching shows the same workspace; reboot survival needs separate configuration.
cards.recovery: Use detach, not exit or kill-session, to leave work running. Cancel a tmux chooser with Esc. Reattach from the same host.

source.label: tmux manual
source.revision: tmux 3.6a concepts; commands rather than guessed keybindings

exercise.goal: Detach from a disposable tmux workspace and return to the same pane.
hints: Choose an expendable session, not a production process or unfamiliar remote host.
From its shell, run tmux detach-client. From the outer shell, run tmux list-sessions.
Run tmux attach-session -t '=YOUR_EXACT_SESSION_NAME', replacing the quoted placeholder with the listed name.
exercise.success: Your pane remains and you can distinguish detach from terminating a session. No progress is stored.

cards.title: Work out which layer receives a shortcut
synonyms: why does this key not work
cards.effect: Identify the receiver before trying a shortcut; terminal settings can intercept keys before tmux or Neovim sees them.
cards.recovery: Esc usually cancels an application picker; it is not a universal undo. Return to the shell before testing shell-specific shortcuts.

source.label: tmux manual
source.revision: tmux 3.6a; private prefix/menu intentionally unresolved without profile

cards.title: Edit, select and undo without losing the file
cards.effect: Edits change the buffer first. Only an explicit write such as :write changes the file on disk.
cards.recovery: Esc returns to Normal mode; u undoes an edit, Ctrl-R redoes it (default mappings). :quit refuses unsaved changes; :quit! discards them deliberately.

source.label: Neovim user manual
source.revision: Neovim 0.11 standard defaults; custom mappings may override them

cards.title: Find files and text in a project
cards.layer: Neovim Normal mode → picker or directory buffer
cards.effect: Distinguish filename, content and recent-file search; Oil can apply filesystem changes if you explicitly save them.
cards.recovery: Cancel a picker with Ctrl-C in Insert or Esc to Normal then Esc. Ctrl-O returns after a jump. Do not write unwanted Oil changes.

source.label: Authored snacks.lua / oil.lua and Neovim quickfix manual
source.revision: Authored source and installed plugin docs inspected 2026-09-06; local bindings require a separate profile

cards.title: Go to definition and navigate code with LSP
cards.layer: Neovim Normal mode; buffer-local LspAttach mappings
cards.effect: Navigation requests information; rename, format and code actions can change buffers or trigger server commands.
cards.recovery: Ctrl-O returns after a jump. Review every affected buffer after edits; undo is buffer-local, not atomic multi-file rollback.

source.label: Authored lsp-config.lua and Neovim LSP manual
source.revision: Authored source and installed lsp.txt inspected 2026-09-06; requires attached capable server

cards.title: Switch buffers and arrange editor windows
cards.layer: Neovim Normal mode; navigator may hand off to tmux
cards.effect: Switch documents or views without confusing a buffer, editor window, tab page or terminal pane.
cards.recovery: Return with :buffer # or Ctrl-W then p. Respect unsaved-change refusals; closing a view does not delete a disk file.

source.label: Authored snacks.lua / nvim-tmux-navigation.lua and Neovim windows manual
source.revision: Authored source and installed windows.txt inspected 2026-09-06; navigator counterpart must be loaded

cards.title: Run nearest test, file or suite deliberately
cards.layer: Neovim Normal mode → vim-test → vimux tmux runner pane
cards.effect: An intentional test run executes project code with possible side effects; TestVisit only navigates. The guide runs nothing.
cards.recovery: Interrupt only the identified runner with Ctrl-C or :VimuxInterruptRunner. Interruption cannot undo test side effects.

source.revision: Plugin commands/strategy inspected 2026-09-06; native terminal reference supplies context, not plugin key defaults

cards.title: Neovim quick reference for everyday editing
cards.layer: Neovim modes, native commands and separately recorded local keys
cards.effect: Recall everyday editing and IDE equivalents while keeping stock defaults separate from personal bindings.
cards.recovery: Esc returns to Normal; u undoes buffer edits. :quit refuses unsaved loss; :quit! deliberately discards it.

cards.title: Split terminal panes and move between them
cards.layer: tmux prefix table, before the shell or editor
cards.effect: Splits and windows start shells; focus and zoom change the view without terminating existing processes.
cards.recovery: Toggle zoom again or move focus back. Detach to preserve work; killing a pane is destructive, not split undo.

cards.title: Copy terminal output and search scrollback
cards.layer: tmux copy-mode-vi versus application input and system clipboard
cards.effect: Copy mode reads pane history into tmux buffers. Pasting sends input to an application and may execute commands.
cards.recovery: Stock vi q exits copy mode; Esc clears selection. Pasted commands and clipboard changes have no general undo.

cards.title: tmux quick reference for keeping work running
cards.layer: tmux prefix/suffix, menu and native commands
cards.effect: Recall session/window/pane actions and distinguish direct key help from the authored menu's full key listing.
cards.recovery: Esc cancels the menu/prompt; q leaves stock vi copy mode. Detach rather than killing work; reconnect on the same host.

cards.title: Choose between a rewrite and feedback
cards.layer: Writing workflow — reference only, not an AI action
cards.effect: Decide the input scope and desired result before using an AI tool. Opening this card sends nothing.
cards.recovery: Keep the original. Discard an unwanted proposal; never paste a critique over the prose. Existing editor AI routes retain their own behavior.

cards.title: Know when to use a cockpit instead of another shell
cards.layer: Personal tools — availability and bindings vary by machine
cards.effect: A cockpit groups personal workflows; a shell builds arbitrary commands. This guide explains the distinction without opening either.
cards.recovery: Use the application's documented quit/back key, or switch tmux windows to leave it running. Do not assume Ctrl-C safely cancels a task already submitted.
